transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Lately I feel like how my body looks and what I weigh are all I can focus on when I think about whether I’m doing well in life. It has just become a really constant thought for me lately.
Do you find yourself eating an unusually large amount of food in a short period, and if so, do you ever feel the need to use methods like vomiting or excessive exercise to prevent weight gain?

No, I don't eat large amounts of food or throw up; it's actually the opposite because I restrict my food heavily, often skipping meals or eating tiny portions. I do jog and do yoga, but I just see that as staying disciplined and healthy. If I do eat something heavy, I panic and cope by cutting back even more the next day instead of vomiting.
How would you describe your weight and body shape right now; do you feel that you are currently at a healthy weight, or do you feel that you are overweight despite what others might say?

My husband and coworkers keep saying I'm too thin and "disappearing," but I honestly feel like they are exaggerating. When I look in the mirror, I still see places around my middle that I need to tighten up to look good in my work uniform and next to the younger dancers in my group. To me, this isn't an unhealthy weight; it just feels like I'm finally being disciplined about my body.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle, such as your periods becoming irregular or stopping altogether, since you began restricting your food intake?
I haven't really noticed any changes or thought much about my menstrual cycle lately. I'm not really sure if my periods have changed at all.
Could you try to recall if it has been more than three months since your last menstrual period?

I honestly can't recall if it's been that long because I haven't been tracking it closely at all. With all the stress of my new promotion and worrying about my parents, my mind has been entirely on other things.
